Access
Sign in to your Apple Account on the Apple Developer website to access basic developer resources. If you’re enrolled in a paid program (the Apple Developer Program or Apple Developer Enterprise Program ), sign in with the Apple Account you used to enroll.

**Two-factor authentication.** In an effort to keep your account more secure, [Two-factor authentication](https://support.apple.com/102660) is required for program Account Holders to sign in to their account. Two-factor authentication or two-step verification is required for all users to sign in to App Store Connect .

To protect your account, always keep your contact information secure and up to date, and never share your Apple Account password or six-digit verification code with anyone. Apple will never ask for this information to provide support. [Learn more](https://support.apple.com/102568) .

**Managed Apple Accounts .** By default, Managed Apple Accounts don’t have access to Apple Developer Program resources.
To enable access, your organization can modify a user’s access in [Apple Business Manager](https://support.apple.com/guide/apple-business-manager/customize-user-access-apps-services-axm53xk34bq/web) or [Apple School Manager](https://support.apple.com/guide/apple-school-manager/customize-user-access-apps-services-axm53xk34bq/1/web/1) .

1. From anywhere on the Apple Developer website, click Account on the top right .

Click your team name on the top right to open the menu, then choose Sign Out.

# From code to customer

Join the Apple Developer Program to reach customers around the world on the App Store for all Apple platforms. Membership provides the tools, resources, and support you need to develop and distribute apps and games, including access to app services, testing tools, app analytics, and more.

## Get the latest betas

Be ready for what’s coming next. Apple customers adopt new software rapidly, so you can keep innovating. Integrate the latest Apple technologies in your apps to deliver incredible experiences on Apple platforms as soon as they’re released.

View the latest releases

## Access comprehensive services and capabilities

Leverage Apple’s tightly integrated hardware, software, services, and capabilities to create useful and engaging experiences.

...

Apple handles worldwide payment processing, offers unlimited hosting and bandwidth — even for free apps — verifies user accounts, and much more. With Apple School Manager and Apple Business, you can offer your app in volume or custom apps only to organizations you specify. You can even choose to distribute your Mac apps outside the Mac App Store using your Developer ID certificate and Apple’s notarization process, reassuring users that you’re a trusted developer.

Learn more about distribution

## Dive deep into analytics

Measure user engagement, marketing campaign performance, monetization, and more in App Store Connect. You’ll get information only Apple provides and no technical implementation is required.

Learn more about App Analytics

## Get help from Apple experts

Join a variety of sessions, appointments, labs, and more — tailored for you.
Meet with Apple activities take place in person and online all over the world, offering you an opportunity to connect directly with Apple engineers and designers — and create your best apps and games yet.

Learn more about Meet with Apple

## Explore benefits

A free Apple developer account gives you access to tools like beta versions of Xcode and operating systems. An Apple Developer membership unlocks all the resources and support you need to build, test, share, and distribute apps and games. Videos, documentation, tutorials, and sample code are available to all.

### Become an Apple developer

Free account

* Access beta versions of Xcode and operating systems
* Test your apps directly on your own devices using Xcode
* Engage on the Apple Developer Forums
* Submit bugs with Feedback Assistant
* Participate in online Meet with Apple events

$99 annual membership

* Includes all Apple developer account benefits
* Access a comprehensive set of developer tools, capabilities, and services
* Invite testers and manage beta builds with TestFlight

* Tap into code-level technical support from Apple experts

Enroll as an individual or organization.

Enroll now

excerpts:
* [prestashop Webinars Learn from experts in live and interactive sessions.](https://twinr.dev/webinars/)

#### [Home](https://twinr.dev/) » [Blogs](https://twinr.dev/blogs/) » Step-by-Step Guide to Enroll in the Apple Developer Program for Businesses

# Step-by-Step Guide to Enroll in the Apple Developer Program for Businesses

By **Gaurav Parvadiya** | Last Updated On July 23rd, 2025

If you want to publish an iOS app for your business – whether it’s a Shopify store, SaaS tool, or anything else – you’ll need to go through Apple’s official route. That means enrolling in the [Apple Developer Program](https://developer.apple.com/programs/) .

But here’s something many people don’t realize: if your app represents a business or brand (not you personally), you must create a **Company or Organization account** . Individual accounts won’t work for business-branded apps, Apple will reject them.
This guide will walk you through the process of how to enroll in Apple Developer Program, and **Apple Developer Program for businesses** step by step. No jargon. No guesswork. Whether you’re using a no-code app builder like Twinr or hiring an agency, enrolling properly is the first step to getting your app on the App Store.

## **What Is the Apple Developer Program (and Why It Matters)**

Apple’s Developer Program is a membership that gives you the tools and permissions to build and distribute iOS apps on the App Store. It costs **$99 per year** and includes:

* Access to **App Store Connect** for uploading and managing your app
* **TestFlight** for internal and beta testing
* Developer tools for managing users, analytics, and push notifications
* Support for **in-app purchases** , subscriptions, and monetization features

According to [Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/263794/number-of-downloads-from-the-apple-app-store/) , as of 2024, the App Store hosts over 1.
8 million apps, making it essential for businesses to comply with **App Store submission requirements** .

More importantly: **your app can’t go live on the App Store without this** .

There are two types of **Apple developer program organization account** :

* **Individual** – for personal apps, not tied to a business
* **Organization** – required if your app is tied to a registered company or brand

If you’re a Shopify store, a registered business, or using a brand name, you’ll need to **enroll business Apple Developer account** if you don’t have one. Now let’s show you how to get one.

## **What You’ll Need Before You Begin (Requirements Checklist)**

Before you start your **Apple Developer account setup** , gather the following **company Apple Developer account requirements** :

### **A D-U-N-S Number**

[This is a unique business ID from Dun & Bradstreet](https://twinr.dev/blogs/how-to-get-duns-number/) . Apple uses it to verify your company is legit.
If you don’t have one, you can request it free at [Apple’s D-U-N-S page](https://developer.apple.com/enroll/duns-lookup/) .

⚠️ Make sure your business name, address, and phone number match your legal documents.

### **A Company Email Address**

Create or use an email that looks professional – for example:  
 you@yourcompany.com  
 Avoid personal Gmail or Yahoo addresses.

### **Apple ID**

### **Legal Business Entity**

Your company must be registered as a legal entity – such as LLC, LLP, Pvt Ltd, or Corporation. Sole proprietors typically don’t qualify for an **Apple Developer Program Organization account** .

### **Authority to Sign Legal Agreements**

Apple will verify that _you_ (the person applying) have the right to act on behalf of the company. You’ll need to be the founder, legal representative, or have a letter of authorization.

**Read More:** [How to Get Your App Featured on Apple’s App Store](https://twinr.
dev/blogs/how-to-get-your-app-featured-on-apple-app-store/)

## **Step-by-Step: Enroll in the Apple Developer Program (Organization Account)**

Follow these steps to learn **how to enroll in Apple Developer Program** . Most of this takes under 30 minutes if you’ve got the details ready.

#### **Step 1: Create an Apple ID (if you don’t have one)**

* Go to [appleid.apple.com](https://appleid.apple.com/)
* Use a business email address
* Add two-factor authentication (Apple requires this for login)

#### **Step 2: Check Your D-U-N-S Number**

* Visit [Apple’s D-U-N-S lookup tool](https://developer.apple.com/enroll/duns-lookup/)
* Enter your business name and address
* If your business doesn’t show up, request a new D-U-N-S (can take 5–7 days)

#### **Step 3: Go to Apple Developer Enrollment**

* Sign in at [developer.apple.com/programs/enroll](https://developer.apple.com/programs/enroll/)
* Choose **“Organization”** when asked for account type
#### **Step 4: Fill in Your Business Details**

* Legal business name
* Website (Apple may verify it)
* Business phone number (you’ll get a verification call)
* Your role in the organization

#### **Step 5: Wait for Apple to Verify Your Info**

* Apple may email or call to confirm your identity and business
* If you’re not the owner, they’ll ask for a signed authorization letter

#### **Step 6: Pay the Annual Fee**

* Once approved, you’ll get a link to pay the **$99/year** fee
* After payment, your membership activates within 24 hours

#### **Step 7: Access App Store Connect**

* Go to [appstoreconnect.apple.com](https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/)
* This is where you’ll upload apps, manage builds, and submit for review

Done! You are now officially enrolled in the **Apple Developer Program.** Just wait for Apple enrollment processing time, which is usually 1 to 4 weeks.

## **Common Mistakes That Delay Approval**

Here are issues many people run into, and how to avoid them:
**1- Using a personal email or Gmail account** **  
** → Use a business domain email instead (like hello@yourbrand.com )

**2- Mismatched business name or address in D-U-N-S** **  
** → Make sure your legal documents, D-U-N-S info, and Apple form match exactly

**3- Not being authorized to enroll** **  
** → Only legal owners or people with written consent can complete the process

**4- Missing website or placeholder domains** **  
** → Apple checks if your site looks legit. Avoid “Coming Soon” pages

**5- Skipping verification steps** **  
** → Always answer Apple’s phone or email within 48 hours to avoid delays

## **How Long Does Enrollment Take?**

Usually, **Apple enrollment processing time** takes **3 to 5 business days** .

* D-U-N-S number issues? Add 5–7 more days
* No response to Apple verification? Add delays
* Wrong business type (like sole prop)? Application may be rejected

To speed things up:

* Use correct business info on first try

...

Once you’re set up, your app is one step away from the App Store – where you can finally unlock push notifications, mobile-first checkout, native loyalty experiences, and everything else your brand deserves.

The process is about **control** . It gives you full ownership over your app, your updates, your users, and your brand identity.

So take the time to do it right. Future-you – and your customers – will thank you.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Do I need a business account for the Apple Developer Program?**

Yes. If your app is for a business, brand, or company (not a personal project), Apple requires that you enroll as an Organization with a D-U-N-S number and legal business entity.

**How much does it cost to join the Apple Developer Program?**

The Apple Developer Program costs $99 per year. This fee gives you access to App Store Connect, developer tools, TestFlight, and app publishing rights.
